for a general p.c.f. set, expressing it formally meets certain

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract says the SG result (a unique HM per degree and boundary data, so that homotopy classes are represented by HMs) extends to p.c.f. fractals. For p.c.f. sets the paper proves no analogue of the homotopy classification, so it never shows that every homotopy class contains a HM. It proves no uniqueness, and the Discussion says uniqueness was not claimed. The homotopy class is controlled only for degrees on a finite cycle basis at one level, and the Discussion says the order of a HM cannot yet be expressed formally. The only p.c.f. result is an existence statement that rests on postulated cycle-embedding and cut-point structure.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, we extend this result to HMs on p.c.f. fractals.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the abstract and introduction to say that for p.c.f. fractals the paper gives only a conditional existence construction for prescribed degrees on a cycle basis, without uniqueness or full homotopy classification.
issues.overall_effect: The headline claim that homotopy classes of maps from p.c.f. fractals to the circle are represented by harmonic maps is not established. Only the SG case is.
issues.title: Abstract claims the SG result (homotopy classes, uniqueness) extends to p.c.f. fractals, but only a conditional existence statement is given
issues.why_classification: No new mathematics is needed, but the advertised p.c.f. generalisation (class representation, uniqueness) is withdrawn, which is a limited loss of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, $F$ is a uniformly continuous function on $\mathcal{P}\times [0,1]$.

issues.failure_explanation: f and g take values in R/Z. The expression t f(x)+(1-t)g(x) mod 1 is not well defined for non-integer t, because it depends on the chosen representatives. The proof silently uses real-valued lifts along each loop and checks closure only for one loop gamma at a time. It never shows that these lifts agree across the different loops of P that share vertices, so that f−g has a single global real lift. This needs the loops partial T_w to generate all cycles of every Gamma_m. The assertion that F is uniformly continuous on P x [0,1] is also given with no estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the homotopy by F(t,x)=g(x)+t h(x) mod 1, where h is a real lift of f−g. Prove that h exists and is continuous, using vanishing degrees on all cell loops, consistency on cycles of the approximating graphs, and uniform continuity.
issues.overall_effect: The 'if' direction of the classification of homotopy classes by the degree vector is not proved as written. The paper's description of HMs as representatives of homotopy classes rests on this direction.
issues.title: Homotopy construction in the converse of the degree-classification theorem is ill-defined and its well-definedness is not proved
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and the repair is a contained lifting argument, but it is a nontrivial missing step, not a routine omission.

issues.failure_explanation: The space hat H fixes only the boundary lift data and rho_0. It contains maps with arbitrary nonzero degrees on sub-cell loops. Lemma lem.minimizer gives uniqueness only among real lifts with a single jump rho_0 at z, that is, only for degree (rho_0,0,0,...). The claim that hat f^* is the unique minimizer over all of hat H is therefore unsupported. Minimizers in other degree classes are different maps, and nothing shows they have larger energy. The monotonicity of the T-valued energies is deduced from a property of real-valued extensions, although T-valued maps need not lift on coarse cells. HMs are defined by Delta f=0, but the argument concludes that hat f^* is a critical point and a minimizer and never links this to Delta f=0 on T-valued maps. Uniqueness among all HMs with the given data and degree vector is therefore not proved. For higher degrees the paper only says 'one can show' the analogue.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the admissible class to maps with the prescribed degree vector. Show that every such map lifts to the cut fundamental domain with the stated jumps. Show that T-valued harmonicity is equivalent to harmonicity of the local lifts, and conclude uniqueness from strict convexity.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness half of the main theorem (and its higher-degree extension) is not established as written. Existence of a lifted harmonic function with the prescribed jumps is fine.
issues.title: Uniqueness of the HM is derived from a minimization over a class that does not fix the higher-order degrees, and harmonic is not shown to mean minimizer
issues.why_classification: The lifting-to-the-covering argument and the harmonic-iff-minimizer step are new lemmas, but they fit the existing covering-space framework and no result is abandoned.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In addition, for every $1\le m\le N$ and $w\in S^m$.

issues.failure_explanation: The sheets are glued with shift l(w), which is the index of the loop, while the jump in H_m^k is rho_{l(w)}. The two descriptions of the covering space disagree. The orientation c_-^k ~ c_+^{k+shift} is also opposite to the jump f(c_+)=f(c_-)+rho. The appendix, meant as the explicit construction, builds cuts only for loops w s with |w|=m>=1. This gives loops of level >=2 and omits the three level-1 loops partial T_1, T_2, T_3. Their degrees rho_1, rho_2, rho_3 are then never realised, although the main text requires cuts for every 0<|w|<=N.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the shift rho_{l(w)} with an orientation consistent with H_m^k, and let the appendix range start at the empty word (m>=0), so that every loop of level 1..N receives a cut.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the explicit covering-space construction for second-order (and higher) HMs does not produce the prescribed degree vector.
issues.title: Cut-point identifications for higher-order maps are inconsistent with the function spaces and the appendix omits level-1 loops
issues.why_classification: The corrections are local re-indexings and a range fix that the surrounding text makes evident, and the method and conclusions are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $K$ is called a p.c.f. fractal if $V_0$ is finite.

issues.failure_explanation: F_w are maps of R^d, so F_w^{-1}(C) contains points outside K. For the SG, F_1^{-m}(y) is the point v_1+2^m(y−v_1). These points are distinct for different m, so V_0 as literally defined is infinite and the SG would not be p.c.f. The standard definition intersects with K, or works with the code-space shift. This contradicts the paper's own use of V_0={v_1,v_2,v_3}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace F_w^{-1}(C) by F_w^{-1}(C ∩ F_w(K)), or use the code-space post-critical set.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of p.c.f. fractal (and V_0 and V_m built from it) is not correct as stated. The later statements about general p.c.f. sets inherit the ambiguity.
issues.title: Definition of V_0 by full preimages of the critical set makes V_0 infinite even for the SG
issues.why_classification: A short standard correction restores the intended definition with no change to results.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We postulate the existence of the embedding
setting with minor modifications, so we highlight only the main distinctions from the previous

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated for an arbitrary p.c.f. K, but its proof needs the cycle embedding iota and the cut points xi satisfying cycle_extend, embed and pcf-cut. These are only postulated in the text and are not in the statement. They are verified in the paper only for figure-based examples. The data are also not shown to be compatible. rho_0 (with an undefined omega_p) is prescribed independently of (rho_1,...,rho_{n_m}), although the outer cycle gamma_0 is an integer combination of basis cycles, which forces a linear relation among the degrees. The boundary condition involving rho_0 is never used in the definition of H_m^k. Uniform continuity and harmonicity across cuts for general harmonic structures are asserted by 'minor modifications'.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the cycle-embedding and cut-point assumptions and the compatibility relation between rho_0, the rho_i and the delta_i as hypotheses of the theorem. Give the omitted continuity and harmonicity argument for the covering construction in the stated generality.

issues.title: p.c.f. existence theorem omits the postulated structural hypotheses and compatibility of degree data, and the proof is only a sketch
issues.why_classification: Making the hypotheses explicit and supplying the contained extension argument yields a recognisably comparable but narrower theorem (the advertised scope is cut from all p.c.f. fractals to those satisfying the postulates).
